hook.line: Hernando tells a story and it matters whether Rosa left before he arrived or just as he came in. One small change of verb decides who was there.
hook.es: Cuando llegué, ya se había ido.
hook.en: When I arrived, he had already left.

examples.es: Cuando Tomás abrió el café, Vale ya había salido.

rule:
Ask one question: which happened first?

Story in order, one thing after another: use the plain past for both. *Cuando llegué, se fue*: I arrived, then he left.

One thing was already done before the other: put that one in *había* plus the ending. *Cuando llegué, ya se había ido*: he left first.

A clue: *ya* and *todavía no* often travel with the earlier event.

And *había* needs another past moment to look back from. On its own, *ayer fui al mercado* is just the plain past.

So the plain past moves the story forward, and *había* steps back.
smallPrint: Teachers call this choosing between the preterite and the pluperfect. The preterite moves the narrative on; the pluperfect marks an event earlier than the one being narrated.

yourTurn.prompt: He was already gone when you got there. Pick and type the whole sentence: *Cuando llegué, ya se ___.* (*fue* or *había ido*) When I arrived, he had already left.
yourTurn.answer: Cuando llegué, ya se había ido.
yourTurn.why: He left before you arrived, so the earlier event takes *había* plus the ending.

yourTurn.prompt: He left just as you arrived. Pick and type the whole sentence: *Cuando llegué, se ___.* (*fue* or *había ido*) When I arrived, he left.
yourTurn.why: One thing after the other, in order, so both verbs use the plain past.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: When Tomás opened the café, Vale had already gone out.
yourTurn.answer: Cuando Tomás abrió el café, Vale ya había salido.
accept: Cuando Tomás abrió el café, ya había salido Vale.
yourTurn.why: Vale went out first, so *había salido*; opening the café is the plain past.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: When I called, Hernando went out.
yourTurn.why: Calling and going out happened in order, so both use the plain past.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: When I called, Hernando still hadn't gone out.
yourTurn.answer: Cuando llamé, Hernando todavía no había salido.
accept: Cuando llamé, Hernando no había salido todavía.
yourTurn.why: Going out had not happened before the call, so *todavía no había salido*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: Hernando told me what had happened.
yourTurn.answer: Hernando me contó lo que había pasado.
accept: Hernando me contó lo que había ocurrido.
yourTurn.why: The telling is the plain past; what had happened came before it.

yourTurn.prompt: Move the second event earlier, with *ya*: *Cuando Vale llegó, Tomás preparó el tinto.*
yourTurn.answer: Cuando Vale llegó, Tomás ya había preparado el tinto.
accept: Cuando Vale llegó, ya había preparado Tomás el tinto.
yourTurn.why: Now the coffee was ready before Vale arrived, so *ya había preparado*.

pitfalls.wrong: Cuando llegué, Vale ya se fue.
pitfalls.right: Cuando llegué, Vale ya se había ido.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *Ya* hints it was done earlier, and that earlier event takes *había* plus the ending.
*Había* needs another past moment to look back from; on its own it's just the plain past.

pitfalls.wrong: Primero había comido y después había salido.
pitfalls.why: Two steps told in order are both plain past; *había* is for the step already done before.

personal: Think of a time you arrived somewhere and someone had already left. Write one sentence starting with *Cuando llegué…* and finish it with what had already happened.
